brief.headline: Lock a modest price cut toward the India export benchmark of ₹42.95/kg and shift to immediate payment in exchange for a ₹1.24 Cr cash rebate, while qualifying Tirupati or Gulshan as a backup source.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a price reduction toward the India export unit value of ₹42.95/kg, targeting a ₹3–5/kg cut from our current ₹66.48/kg.
priceAsk.target: Move closer to the ₹42.95/kg India export benchmark, aiming for ₹61–63/kg
priceAsk.basis: The market asks for Anhydrous Dextrose IP sit in a ₹60–81/kg band (typical ₹66–73/kg), and our ₹66.48/kg is already rated MARKET-FAIR (slightly favourable). The India export line is ₹42.95/kg, showing room to negotiate downward. We are their sole listed customer with ₹15.03 Cr annual spend, giving us weight to ask for a better deal.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to move from 30 Days After Receipt to immediate payment (advance or on-delivery) in return for a rebate.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Shifting to immediate payment frees up ₹1.24 Cr of our cash that is currently tied up in the 30-day cycle — we should ask for a rebate equal to that figure, paid as a one-time credit or spread across the year.

brief.financialLeverage: Sayaji publishes no financial statements, so we have no window into their profit margins, cash position or debt load. That means we cannot gauge how hard to press without risking their stability. Our ₹15.03 Cr spend is material for any mid-sized starch producer, so we have buying power. The safest play is to anchor the price ask to the public export benchmark and the market-ask data, and to build a second source (Tirupati, Gulshan or Sanstar) so we are not flying blind on Sayaji's health.

evidence.point: We spend ₹15.03 Cr annually with Sayaji
Our current Dextrose price is ₹66.48/kg, which sits in the typical market band but above the India export reference
The market verdict is MARKET-FAIR (slightly favourable), with a typical ask of ₹66–73/kg
evidence.figure: ₹60–81/kg ask band, typical ₹66–73/kg, verdict MARKET-FAIR (slightly favourable)

evidence.point: Paying Sayaji earlier frees up ₹1.24 Cr of our cash
Sayaji's financials are not public, so we cannot assess their margins or cash tightness

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore maize wet-miller making Dextrose ANHYDROUS (IV-fluid grade) — exact form match; confirm IP monograph CoA before switching.

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker; established dextrose/sorbitol supplier — a drop-in alternate to Sayaji.

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (starch, dextrose) — growing capacity.

risks: Sayaji's finances are invisible, so we do not know if they are profitable or stretched — pushing too hard on price could destabilise a key supplier.
We are already at a MARKET-FAIR price (₹66.48/kg vs typical ₹66–73/kg), so the room for a cut is narrow unless we benchmark to the export line.
Asking for immediate payment and a rebate simultaneously may meet resistance; be ready to stage the asks or settle for one.
None of the alternates are qualified yet — start an RFQ with Tirupati and Gulshan immediately so we have real backup pricing before the next Sayaji renewal.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, and with ₹15.03 Cr annual spend we'd like to align our Dextrose price closer to the India export benchmark of ₹42.95/kg and explore a rebate if we move to faster payment.
